title: Neuromuscular, cardiovascular, and cognitive fatigue in motor learning: A systematic review
title_zh: 运动学习中的神经肌肉、心血管与认知疲劳：系统综述
abstract: BACKGROUND: Fatigue is multifactorial and task-dependent, arising from the interplay between performance and perceived fatigability. Fatigue-related changes in sensorimotor control and neural activity may alter skill acquisition and retention. OBJECTIVE: To synthesize behavioral and neurophysiological evidence on how cognitive, cardiovascular, local neuromuscular, and mixed fatigue influence motor-skill acquisition, retention, and transfer. METHODS: A systematic search was conducted within PubMed, Web of Science, and Embase. Thirty-eight articles, corresponding to 43 extracted experiments, met inclusion criteria. Data were extracted on fatigue protocol, learning taxonomy, learning stage, retention/transfer context, fatigue asssessment, and neurophysiology. Methodological quality was appraised with a modified Downs and Black checklist. RESULTS: During acquisition, 28 of 43 experiments (65.1%) showed detrimental effects, 4 (9.3%) showed facilitatory effects, 7 (16.3%) showed neutral effects, and 4 (9.3%) were mixed or inconclusive. Retention after recovery and retention under sustained or renewed fatigue were assessed in 36 and 7 experiments, respectively. Retention findings were variable and depended on fatigue modality, task demands, and testing context. Neurophysiological measures were scarce, being included in only six experiments, and sex-specific analyses or other participant-level moderators were rarely examined. CONCLUSIONS: Fatigue does not uniformly impair motor learning. Local neuromuscular fatigue appears most likely to disrupt acquisition and sometimes retention, whereas cardiovascular exertion may support learning or consolidation in some contexts when acute fatigue has partly recovered. Evidence for cognitive fatigue remains limited and inconsistent. Future work should use standardized fatigue assessment, longer retention windows, state-matched testing, and integrated neurophysiology to clarify mechanisms and guide training under fatigue.
abstract_zh: 背景：疲劳是多因素且任务依赖的，源于表现疲劳度与主观疲劳感的交互。疲劳相关的感觉运动控制和神经活动改变可能影响技能获得与保持。目的：综合行为学与神经生理学证据，系统总结认知、心血管、局部神经肌肉及混合性疲劳对运动技能学习、保持与迁移的影响。方法：在PubMed、Web of Science和Embase中进行系统检索。共有38篇文章（对应43个提取实验）符合纳入标准。我们提取了疲劳范式、学习分类、学习阶段、保持/迁移情境、疲劳评估与神经生理学等信息，并使用修订版Downs与Black量表评估方法学质量。结果：在习得阶段，43个实验中有28项（65.1%）显示不利影响，4项（9.3%）显示促进作用，7项（16.3%）无明显效应，4项（9.3%）结果混合或不一致。恢复后保持和持续或重新疲劳下的保持在36项与7项实验中分别被评估。保持效应存在较大变异，取决于疲劳类型、任务需求及测试情境。神经生理指标应用稀少，仅有6项实验纳入；性别特异性分析及其他受试者层面调节因素也很少。结论：疲劳并非对运动学习一律有害。局部神经肌肉疲劳最可能破坏习得并有时影响保持，而心血管负荷在急性疲劳部分恢复后，在某些情境下可支持学习或巩固。认知疲劳的证据仍有限且不一致。未来研究应采用标准化疲劳评估、延长保持时间窗、状态匹配的测试范式，并整合神经生理学指标，以澄清机制并指导疲劳状态下的训练设计。
